NO. 015 · Songbirds & City Birds / Sturnidae · Starlings & Mynas

Crested Myna

八哥 · bā gē Acridotheres cristatellus
Resident Common 25–28 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A tuft on the forehead, and an 'eight' in flight

Entirely black, with a tuft of feathers standing up from the forehead like a small pompadour. In flight the white wing patches open into a figure of eight — the name is more literal than you would expect. It is one of the south's best talkers.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • ForeheadA tuft of black feathers projecting forward and up from the forehead — the key difference from other mynas.
  • ColourAll black with metallic green-blue gloss in sunlight; eye orange-yellow; bill ivory or pale yellow.
  • Wing patchWhite bases to the primaries, showing as a thin white edge when perched and as a clear white 'eight' in flight.
  • TailWhite tips to the tail feathers, visible from below when perched and obvious in flight.

Behaviour

Mostly terrestrial, striding across lawns, fields and roadsides for insects, earthworms and fruit; also feeds around cattle and rubbish bins. Bold and thoroughly at home in dense city. A gifted mimic — caged birds learn speech and whistles, wild ones imitate other birds and mechanical sounds. Nests in wall cavities, tree holes and the gaps inside billboards.

Voice

Field recording
Tap the waveform to seek · headphones recommended
0:00 / 0:09
Recording iNaturalist user skystargazer · Licence CC BY-NC · Original file

Loud and harsh, usually a mix of 'ji-ji-ji' and 'kia-kia', with pleasant whistles and imitations. A flock calling at dawn in a tree is startlingly loud.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen farmland
  • Jinwan grassland
  • around city refuse stations
  • Tangjiawan rooftops
Field note
Versus Black-collared Starling: the Crested Myna is all black with an ivory bill; the starling has a black head and breast but a white belly and a ring of orange-yellow bare skin around the eye.
